summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, steroid dependence, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for recurrent symptomatic hypotension following an inability to obtain his prescribed rescue dexamethasone due to a pharmacy back order. He presented with dizziness, slurred speech, and chest pain, preceded by a three-day history of diarrhea consistent with an IBD flare. His hypotension was attributed to relative adrenal insufficiency and gastrointestinal fluid losses. He was treated with IV fluids, IV dexamethasone, and oral and IV potassium repletion. His prednisone dose was increased from 10 mg to 20 mg daily, and a new rescue plan with hydrocortisone 100 mg IM via Act-o Vial was established. His potassium normalized, diarrhea improved, and blood pressure stabilized. He was discharged home with medication adjustments, including liquid potassium supplementation and instructions to titrate torsemide based on edema and blood pressure, with follow-up planned in endocrinology and pain clinic.
